00The answer
In one page

Most agencies would have to go and rent what Uber is asking for. We already own it.

AD PRO owns and operates fifty-eight digital LED screens across the ten cities named in this RFP, runs its own printing, fabrication and installation, and files its own permissions with the city corporations, RAJUK, DMTCL, the Railway, Civil Aviation and the police. That single fact answers the two criteria this RFP weights most heavily — and it is why our commercial proposal can do something a reseller's cannot.

Zero markup, and on our own screens, zero pass-through Third-party media, government fees and production are billed at documented actuals with no markup and no handling fee. On the fifty-eight screens we own there is no third party to pass through at all — Uber pays the operator's rate because we are the operator.
No retainer, no account-management fee The dedicated team, the permissions desk and all reporting are carried in our margin on work delivered. Uber pays for media and production, not for the privilege of being a client.
Nothing goes up without two approvals Uber's written approval and the external permission, both on file, before a single fixing is drilled. Every installation is handed over with its permission pack.
Proof of display inside 24 hours Dated, geo-referenced photographs of every site, plus the played-spot log for digital, delivered within a day of going live.
We already advertise for the authorities The Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Planning, Bangladesh Army, Bangladesh Air Force, Ansar & VDP, DGHS and the Department of Fisheries are existing AD PRO clients. Permission work is not a department we would be building for Uber.
Uber's paper, accepted as it stands NET60 accepted. Purchase-order discipline accepted. The MSA and SOW template is accepted without redlines, and the MNDA is returned with this submission.

4.1Company profile

An advertising company that also happens to be a manufacturer.

Ad Pro Communications Ltd. is a Bangladeshi out-of-home advertising company incorporated in Dhaka on 31 October 2019. We plan, own, build, install and report outdoor media. The distinction that matters for this RFP is that we are not an intermediary: the screens are ours, the printing presses and fabrication shop are ours, the installation crews are on our payroll, and the permission files are opened in our name.

Our mission is to keep clients competitive with marketing that is proven rather than fashionable. Our vision is to raise the standard of outdoor advertising in Bangladesh — which begins with never installing anything that is not fully permitted.

4.4Government liaison and permissions

The part of this contract that goes wrong is the part we do in-house.

Unauthorised branding in Bangladesh is not a paperwork problem. It is a removal, a fine, a photograph of a competitor's hoarding where yours used to be, and a conversation with a city corporation that then remembers your brand. That is the risk this RFP is really buying against, and it is the reason permission capability is weighted more heavily here than execution or price.

AD PRO does not subcontract this. We maintain a standing liaison desk that files in our own name, because every one of our fifty-eight sites is held under permissions we obtained and renew ourselves. The same desk, the same people and the same relationships would carry Uber's filings.

The evidence pack

Before any installation, Uber receives a single PDF per site containing: the written permission, licence or NOC with its reference number and validity; the media-owner or property-owner agreement; the approved artwork proof against Uber's brand guidelines; the site survey photograph with dimensions; and the government or authority fee receipt at face value. No fixing is drilled until Uber has that pack and has said yes in writing.

The Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Planning, the Bangladesh Army, the Bangladesh Air Force, Bangladesh Ansar & VDP, the Directorate General of Health Services, the Department of Fisheries and the Deputy Commissioner's Office, Manikganj are existing AD PRO clients. Client names, campaign photographs and referee contacts for each are available on request, subject to the confidentiality we owe those clients — the same confidentiality Uber is entitled to from us.

4.8How a campaign runs

From brief to closure report, with a gate Uber controls.

  • Brief and site surveyUber gives the city, the dates and the objective. We survey candidate sites and return photographs, exact dimensions, facing, traffic context and the permitting authority for each.
  • Permission filingFiled in AD PRO's name within 48 hours of site approval. Government and authority fees are quoted at face value with the receipt to follow.
  • Uber's written approval — the gateUber approves the site, the artwork and the cost in writing. Nothing is produced or installed before this, and nothing is installed before the external permission is also in hand. Both are held on file.
  • ProductionPrinting, fabrication and pre-flight against Uber's brand guidelines in our own facility. Proof to Uber within 48 hours of final artwork.
  • InstallationOur crews, our safety method statement, road clearance where needed. Installed inside the agreed campaign window.
  • Proof of display within 24 hoursDated, geo-referenced photographs of every site; played-spot logs for digital screens.
  • Monitoring and maintenanceRoutine checks by the divisional executive. Damaged, incorrect or non-functioning material attended within 24 hours and replaced at our cost where the fault is ours.
  • Removal, restoration and closureBranding removed and the site restored at campaign end. Closure report with photographs, permission documents and full cost reconciliation against every purchase order.

The operator's rate, and nothing added to anyone else's.

5.6Transparency declaration

Zero markup, in writing.

AD PRO Communications Ltd. undertakes that all government fees, media-owner charges and third-party costs incurred on Uber Bangladesh's behalf will be billed to Uber as pass-through actuals at zero markup, each supported by the corresponding quotation, invoice or official receipt.

No handling fee, markup or commission is proposed anywhere in this response. Should any circumstance ever warrant one, AD PRO will state the reason in writing, provide documentation showing the cost break-up, and obtain Uber's prior written agreement before the cost is incurred — as Part 3 of the RFP requires.

On the fifty-eight LED screens AD PRO owns and operates there is no third-party cost to pass through at all. Uber is quoted the operator's rate directly.
